# House rule book

_Rewritten after UW-T30. Every entry is reviewer-settled practice from an application already decided in this run (UW-T01 through UW-T30). The starter manual governs anything this book is silent on; where the two differ, the book records the reviewer's practice and the book wins._

_The book departs from a plain reading of the manual's tables in six places: private aviation takes a first-band flat extra rather than the fallback debit (10); a hazardous avocation beside a class C occupation is carved out by exclusion rider rather than charged (9); family-history debits are dropped once the applicant is older than 60 (7); a treated blood pressure carries the treatment charge alone, neither topped up nor credited away (4); where the cholesterol band and the ratio band disagree the ratio governs and the cholesterol band is not charged (5); four or more charged cardiac tables carry an interaction charge on top of their own debits (15). Three further points sit on top of the manual rather than against it: cover above the income multiple postpones the file (1), a DUI within the last two years postpones it (2), with the rest of the file still worked underneath (20); and late-onset well-controlled type 2 diabetes is charged on its A1c and then credited one band (6). Everything else is the manual's tables charged exactly as written._

_Ten files in a row - UW-T21 through UW-T30 - have been confirmed by working this book and adding nothing to it. UW-T30 is the latest: $2,500,000 applied for on a $52,000 income, postponed on the multiple, with a treated blood pressure the only line that would have charged and the two of them the whole driver list. It is the reminder that entry 1 decides the file before a single medical reading is looked at, and that a postponed file still names what would have rated._

## How to use this book

Work every file in this order, and write one line for each step.

1. **Postponement checks (1 and 2).** Total cover against the income multiple; any DUI and its year. Both run on every file, before any table. If either trips, the decision is `postpone`, rating class null, modifiers empty - and you still work the rest of the file (20). Where neither trips, say so in one line and go to the tables.
2. **Referred lines (16).** List every line the manual sends to underwriting judgement and check which are actually live; the manual's referral words are narrow, and a line outside them is simply charged on its table. Resolve each live line under its own entry, and follow the entry instead of the manual's table, instead of the manual's fallback, and instead of your own reasoning.
3. **Tables, interaction, class.** Charge each table on the reading as entries 3 to 14 leave it. Count the charged cardiac tables and add the interaction at four or more (15). Take any late-onset diabetes credit (6). Read the class off the manual's bands (18), or work the preferred criteria where every table is zero (17).
4. **Drivers (19).** The reviewer checks the material factors as closely as the class: a correct class with a wrong list is still a mismatch, and a correct list does not save a wrong class.

## 1. Total cover against the income multiple

**When it applies:** every file, before any table. Face amount applied for plus cover already in force, against the section 14 multiple for the applicant's age: 18-30 30x | 31-40 25x | 41-50 20x | 51-60 15x (60 included) | 61+ 10x. In-force cover always counts in full; nothing in force means the face amount alone is the total.

**Inside the multiple:** say so in one line - total, multiple, ceiling - and go on to the tables. Not a judgement item, not a driver, never a postponement. UW-T29: $250,000 applied for plus $250,000 in force against a 15x ceiling of $1,275,000 on an income of $85,000; one line, and the file rated normally.

**Outside the multiple:** decision `postpone`, rating class null, modifiers empty. Say the file is postponed for financial evidence - justification of the amount, income verification, purpose of cover - and state the total, the multiple and the excess. Then finish the file under entry 20. Name 'face amount to income' among the drivers.

**Boundary:** do the multiplication, never the impression. No tolerance above the multiple is known; do not invent one, and the size of the excess changes nothing - a fifth over and two and a half times over are the same postponement. UW-T02 overshot a 25x ceiling by under a fifth on an otherwise clean Standard; UW-T28 stood at $1,600,000 against a 10x ceiling of $600,000; UW-T30 at $2,600,000 against a 20x ceiling of $1,040,000 on a $52,000 income. All three were postponed. A high face amount on a high income can be inside; a moderate one can be far outside once the band drops. The shape to catch is a large face beside a modest income, and the way to catch it is to do this sum first, before a clean medical picture makes the file look easy.

**Why:** UW-T02 was accepted with a paragraph on why the excess was tolerable and the reviewer postponed it; UW-T28 and UW-T30 were postponed from the start and confirmed whole. Whether the amount is justified is not answered by anything else on the file, and nothing in the medical picture announces it.

## 2. DUI

**When it applies:** a DUI conviction appears on the file.

**Within two years of the application - postpone.** Settled at one year (a 2025 conviction on a 2026 file, UW-T24) and at two (2024 on 2026, UW-T06 and UW-T09). Decision `postpone`, class null, modifiers empty: no rider or flat extra is sent even where entry 9 or 10 would have attached one, though the avocation is still named. Say the file is postponed for the conviction to age and for the record around it - disposition, licence status, any alcohol assessment or treatment - and that liver chemistry, normal or raised, and an empty alcohol history settle the question neither way. Then finish the file under entry 20 and name 'DUI'.

**Older than two years:** charge the manual's rate, name 'DUI', and say judgement was used on recency. Three years is untested: lean recent, postpone, and say judgement was used, because both corrections on this line were for accepting too soon.

**Boundary:** it trips on its own. A clean MVR or three violations, normal enzymes or enzymes above twice normal, no alcohol history, a class C occupation with a hazardous avocation beside it, a light file or a heavy one - none of these switches it off or turns it back into a rating. Moving violations are a separate line (12) and never a reason to postpone. No DUI on the file means this entry has nothing to act on however many violations sit beside it (UW-T29: one violation, no DUI, nothing to say). The two postponement checks are independent: either can trip alone - UW-T30 was postponed on the multiple with a spotless record - and both are always written down.

**Why:** UW-T06 accepted a 2024 conviction at Table 4 and was postponed on review; UW-T09 and UW-T24 were postponed from the start and confirmed whole. Recency is settled by time, and nothing on today's file stands in for it.

## 3. Build

**When it applies:** every file; section 3.

**Stable weight:** not a recent change in build, not referred. Read the printed BMI off the section 3 band - 19.0 to 27.9 zero and unnamed; 28.0 to 30.9 the first charged band; 31.0 to 33.9 the second; higher bands likewise. A BMI at the top of a band is still in that band (30.1 is the first band, not the second). Where the band charges, name 'build'. UW-T29: BMI 29.9 with no change over twelve months, first charged band, 'build' named and confirmed; UW-T23 at 28.3, UW-T25 at 30.1 and UW-T20 at 30.6 the same. UW-T30 at 24.0, weight stable, was the zero band and went unmentioned.

**Weight lost in the last twelve months:** this is the section 3 referral and it is settled. Add half the year's loss back onto the current weight, recompute the BMI at the file's height, and read the band off the recomputed figure. One sentence: weight down so many pounds, half added back under judgement, adjusted weight and BMI so much, band read accordingly. Do it whichever way it moves the file, including where the printed BMI is in the zero band and the add-back puts a charge on it (UW-T17). Never name 'weight change' or 'weight loss'; the driver is 'build'.

**Boundary:** half is the fraction settled at a 16 lb, a 17 lb and a 28 lb loss; do not scale it. Zero change over twelve months is stable and there is nothing to add back. Weight gained in the year is untested: read the current BMI, subtract nothing, say judgement was used. Do not credit a loss and do not postpone for the weight to prove stable. Stature and frame change nothing either way - a short stature does not soften a charged BMI and a tall frame adds nothing to a zero-band one. Build on the adjusted weight is a cardiac table (15) and is the figure the preferred criteria are read against.

**Why:** UW-T10's markup settled the add-back and UW-T14 and UW-T17 repeated it word for word, the class rising both times and confirmed. Recent loss is not yet durable; a stable weight is what it says it is.

## 4. Blood pressure

**When it applies:** every file; section 4.

**Untreated:** charge the worse of the systolic and diastolic bands - one charge, never two - and name 'blood pressure reading'. The zero band runs to 138 systolic and 88 diastolic, so a reading in the 130s is nothing and unnamed. UW-T29: 144/85 untreated, the systolic in the first charged band and the diastolic in the zero band, the worse of the two charged once and 'blood pressure reading' named, confirmed. UW-T20 at 148/84 and UW-T09 at 147/83 the same.

**On treatment:** charge the on-treatment debit and nothing else, whatever the reading and whatever year treatment began. Do not read the untreated table against a treated reading - a treated 143/84 whose systolic would have charged untreated still carries the treatment debit alone (UW-T30) - and do not credit the treatment charge to zero because the reading is controlled: that is how the manual's referral for a treated condition now at target resolves. Name 'blood pressure treatment', never 'blood pressure reading'. Do not write that a reading like 140/85 on treatment is off target. One sentence: treated since such a year, referred, judgement used, the treatment charge stands alone and the reading is not charged on top.

**Boundary:** a treated reading from about 149 systolic or 95 diastolic is untested - charge the treatment debit, say judgement was used on whether the reading charges on top, and do not add it without a case. How long the applicant has been treated changes nothing: treatment begun in 2019 on a 2026 file is the same charge as treatment begun last year. Any treatment closes all three preferred classes. On a zero-debit file an untreated reading is read against the preferred criteria as two figures, each against its own limit (17). Blood pressure, treated or charged untreated, is one cardiac table (15); on a postponed file it is a would-have-charged line and goes on the driver list as 'blood pressure treatment' (UW-T30).

**Why:** UW-T17 charged the treatment debit but named the reading and called it off target; the reviewer's factor was 'blood pressure treatment' and the markup settled that treated and controlled pressure carries the treatment charge only. UW-T22 applied it as the sole charge at Standard and was confirmed whole; UW-T30 applied it as the only would-have-charged line under a postponement and the reviewer's two-factor list carried it.

## 5. Lipids: total cholesterol and the ratio

**When it applies:** every file; section 5. Put the total cholesterol on its band (up to 240 zero | 241-280 first | 281-320 second | 321+ third) and the ratio on its band (up to 5.0 zero | 5.1-6.5 first | 6.6+ second), and compare the two bands. Both tables are in force.

**Both in the zero band:** charge nothing, name nothing, even where the HDL is low or the figures closed a preferred class. A cholesterol well into the 220s is still the zero band: UW-T30's 225 against a ratio of 4.6 charged nothing and named nothing, both figures sitting above a Preferred threshold and that changing nothing.

**Both in the same charged band:** the tables agree and nothing is referred. Charge both and name 'total cholesterol' and 'lipid ratio' as two drivers. UW-T29: cholesterol 256 and ratio 6.1, both in the first charged band, both charged and both named, confirmed; UW-T04 and UW-T09 the same. Both in the second band is untested: charge both, name both, say judgement was used.

**In different bands:** this is the section 5 referral, and it is settled - the ratio governs. Charge the ratio's band and nothing for total cholesterol. Name 'lipid ratio' only where the ratio's band charges, and never 'total cholesterol'. Where the ratio's band is zero the lipid line charges nothing and names nothing at all: cholesterol 263 against a ratio of 3.9 (UW-T24) was charged nothing and neither lipid factor reached the reviewer's list. One sentence: cholesterol such, ratio such, bands disagree, judgement used, the ratio governs and the cholesterol band is not charged. Do not charge both and write that judgement was used (UW-T18), do not charge the worse, do not split the difference.

**Boundary:** settled disagreements all run cholesterol above ratio - 323 against 5.3 and 329 against 5.7 were each charged the first band, not the third. A cholesterol of 321 or more can never agree with the ratio. The ratio above the cholesterol has no case yet: the ratio governs, charge its band, say judgement was used. A low HDL is never a factor of its own and a high HDL is not a credit; both are already inside the ratio. The lipid line is two cardiac tables when both bands charge, one when only the ratio charges, and none when the ratio governs to nothing or both bands are zero (15).

**Why:** UW-T18 charged both on disagreeing bands and came out one step too severe; the reviewer settled that the ratio governs. UW-T29 shows the other half of the rule: where the two bands agree, the manual's two tables simply both charge and both are named.

## 6. A1c and diabetes

**When it applies:** every file; section 6.

**No diabetes diagnosis:** the A1c is charged on its table with no credit, whatever the reading, and the late-onset credit below never applies. In the zero band (up to 6.4) it is nothing and unnamed, even where it misses a preferred threshold; UW-T30 at 5.1 went unmentioned. In a charged band, charge as written and name 'A1c'. UW-T29: A1c 6.8 with no diagnosis, charged as written, no credit, named, confirmed; UW-T09 and UW-T20 the same at 6.8, UW-T04 at 6.6. The absence of a diagnosis is not a credit.

**Type 2 diabetes first diagnosed in later middle age and well controlled:** the section 6 referral. Charge the A1c on its table, take a credit against the total for late-onset well-controlled disease, and read the class one band below what the uncredited total reads. Name two drivers, 'A1c' and 'late-onset diabetes credit'. One sentence: diagnosed in such a year at such an age, controlled by such means to such an A1c; charged as written; credit of one band taken under judgement; size is judgement.

**Size of the credit:** one band, at the bottom of the ladder as in the middle. Settled where an uncredited 200 read Table 6 (UW-T10, UW-T17) and where an uncredited 50 read Standard (UW-T26). Do not scale it for a heavier or lighter file, and do not withhold it because the uncredited class already looks fair.

**Boundary:** ages at diagnosis of 49, 49 and 54 are settled, so from about 45 take the credit and say judgement was used on the age; the twenties or thirties are not later middle age. The whole 6.5-6.9 band under diet is well controlled; oral medication in that band is untested - the condition is control, not means, so take the credit and say so. 7.0 or above with a diagnosis is untested: charge, take no credit. A diagnosed diabetic at 6.4 or under has nothing to charge or credit, but the diagnosis still closes all three preferred classes. A credited A1c is still a charged cardiac table (15), and the credit is local: it softens no other line and no other line withdraws it.

**Why:** UW-T10 was corrected to take the credit; UW-T17 withheld it by drawing the age line at the early fifties and lost a band; UW-T26 took it from the start where the A1c was the only charge and was confirmed at Standard with those two drivers. Do not draw the age line tight again.

## 7. Family history

**When it applies:** a parent or sibling had an MI, stroke or cancer before age 60, so section 8 would charge it.

**Applicant 60 or under:** charge per event, capped as the manual caps it, and name 'family history'. At exactly 60 the applicant is not older than 60: charge, and say judgement was used.

**Applicant older than 60:** the referral for applicants past the qualifying age wins over the table's line that the applicant's own age never changes the charge. Drop the debit, do not name it, and say in one sentence that the applicant is past the qualifying age and the family-history debits are dropped under judgement. Settled at 63 with two events, 65 with one and 68 with two.

**Boundary:** two events cap before the drop and are dropped as readily as one; the kind of event and the site of a cancer change nothing. Do not postpone for records. A dropped line is not a charged cardiac table (15) and is not a driver, even on a postponed file. On a zero-debit file a dropped event still counts against the preferred criteria: one closes Preferred and Preferred Plus, two close Standard Plus as well. No event on the file means nothing to act on at any age and meets the family criterion of every preferred class (UW-T29 and UW-T30: nothing before 60 in parents or siblings, unmentioned).

**Why:** UW-T13, UW-T20 and UW-T28 all dropped the events and were confirmed, the reviewer's lists carrying no family line. An applicant who has lived past the age that defines an early event has outrun the risk the charge prices.

## 8. Tobacco

**When it applies:** every file; section 7.

**Never used, or quit more than five years ago:** zero and unnamed, and a negative nicotine screen beside it is unmentioned. Never used meets the tobacco criterion of every preferred class; quit over five years meets Preferred and Standard Plus but never Preferred Plus. UW-T29 and UW-T30: never used, screen negative, nothing said and nothing named.

**Quit one to five years ago:** charge as written and name 'tobacco'. The negative screen confirms the declaration and nothing more - not a credit, not a driver, not a judgement item. The debit closes all three preferred classes.

**Current use, or a nicotine-positive result against a declared never:** the manual's smoker rule - add the smoker debit and cap the best available class at Standard. Untested; rate as the manual writes and say so.

**Boundary:** tobacco is not a cardiac table, and it is charged and named however light or heavy the rest of the file: on UW-T28 it was the only line on the whole file that would have charged and it still went on the driver list beside the postponement.

**Why:** the reviewer has named 'tobacco' on every file carrying a quit-within-five-years declaration (UW-T02, UW-T08, UW-T10, UW-T11, UW-T16, UW-T18, UW-T20, UW-T21, UW-T28), the screen negative and unmentioned each time it was on the file.

## 9. Occupation class, and class C beside a hazardous avocation

**When it applies:** every file for section 9, and the section 10 referral where a class C occupation sits with an avocation section 10 would charge - amateur motorsport, private aviation, scuba beyond 60 ft, technical rock or ice climbing.

**Occupation alone:** read the class off the manual's own lists, not off how the job sounds. Class A is zero - charge nothing, name nothing (UW-T29: office administrator; UW-T30: pharmacist, both class A on the manual's list and both unmentioned). Class B and class C charge as written and are named 'occupation class'. No class is a referred item on its own: nothing about judgement, no softening because the rest of the file is clean, no adding because the work sounds dangerous. Class B always carries a debit, so the Standard Plus criterion that admits class B is never met in practice. Occupation class is not a cardiac table.

**Class C with a hazardous avocation declared:** charge the occupation class debit as written; for the avocation attach an exclusion rider (type exclusion, amount_per_1000 null) whose detail names the hazard excluded - 'technical rock climbing', 'amateur motorsport' - and charge no avocation debits and no flat extra. The rider makes the decision `accept_with_modification` and does not move the class, which is read off the debits alone. Name 'occupation class' and the avocation by its short name, 'climbing' or 'motorsport': the avocation is material though it carries no charge. One sentence: class C with such an avocation is referred, judgement used, occupation class charged as written, the avocation carved out by exclusion rider, no avocation debits. How often the applicant pursues it changes nothing.

**Boundary:** the rider needs a section 10 avocation actually declared. A class C occupation with 'avocation: none' is the occupation alone - charge as written, send no modifier, and the decision is `accept` if nothing else modifies it (UW-T25, confirmed). Do not go looking in the 'also on file' line for the avocation (11). On a postponed file the rider is not sent but the avocation is still named (UW-T24).

**Why:** UW-T01's motorsport flat extra was struck and replaced by an exclusion rider; UW-T23 applied the rider from the start and was confirmed whole with four factors; UW-T24 named the avocation under a postponement. Once one hazardous exposure is priced through the occupation class, a second is removed from cover rather than charged on top - and where there is no second, there is nothing to remove.

## 10. Private aviation with a class A or B occupation

**When it applies:** the applicant flies as a private pilot and the occupation is not class C. This replaces the manual's fallback debit.

**What to do:** no debits for aviation on any table. Attach a flat extra at the first band (amount_per_1000 2.50) with the detail naming private aviation. Decision `accept_with_modification`; the class is read off the other tables and the flat extra moves it neither up nor down. Name 'aviation'. Say aviation was considered under judgement, the hours are modest, and it carries a first-band flat extra and no rating debits. Never decline for the flying alone.

**Boundary:** modest hours are settled at 77 and 82 a year on logbooks in the hundreds or low thousands of total hours. A heavier programme, aerobatics or a very thin logbook is untested: still no debits, still a flat extra, say judgement was used on the band and do not step up without a case. With a class C occupation, entry 9 converts the avocation to a rider instead. Aviation is not a cardiac table, and a pilot's file never reaches a preferred class because every preferred class requires no hazardous avocation. 'Avocation: none' means there is nothing to do here (UW-T25 through UW-T30).

**Why:** UW-T10 charged the fallback debit and came out one step too severe, the reviewer replacing it with a first-band flat extra; UW-T21 applied the rule at Standard and was confirmed with tobacco and aviation the material factors.

## 11. Other avocations, and pastimes that are not avocations

**When it applies:** an avocation is declared, or a pastime appears in the file's 'also on file' line.

**A section 10 avocation beside a class A or B occupation,** other than aviation, is untested: charge as the table reads - technical climbing its debit, scuba by maximum depth, amateur motorsport a $5.00 flat extra - name the avocation, and say so.

**A pastime section 10 does not list is not an avocation.** It carries nothing, is never named, is never hunted for, and does not close the 'no hazardous avocation' criterion of any preferred class. Settled across stained glass, chillies, first-edition crime novels, a book club, a pub quiz, classical guitar, beekeeping, sourdough, a rugby season ticket, Saturday volunteering at a food bank, pets, tropical fish - and on UW-T30 a community choir, left unmentioned on a postponed file that declared no avocation and was confirmed whole. Keeping bees is not an avocation even where the file prints 'avocation: none' beside it, and on a postponed file an unlisted pastime is simply left unmentioned like any other.

**Why:** the 'also on file' line has been incidental on every file that carried one (UW-T21 through UW-T30). Do not reason a hobby into a hazard, or steadiness of character into a rating.

## 12. Driving record: moving violations

**When it applies:** every file; section 11.

**What to do:** zero or one violation in the last three years is the zero band - charge nothing, name nothing (UW-T29: one violation, unmentioned; UW-T30: none, unmentioned even under a postponement). Two is the first charged band and three or more the second: charge as written and name 'moving violations'. A DUI is its own line (2), and where both sit on the file both are named, the violations named beside a postponement as a would-have-charged line.

**Boundary:** violations are never a referred item and never a reason to postpone, whatever the count: three in three years is the second charged band, not the manual's 'recent motoring conviction', which is the DUI line. Two or more carry a debit, so the file never reaches a preferred class. A single violation on an otherwise zero-debit file leaves it at Standard by criterion; beside a charge elsewhere it is nothing. A clean record with no DUI is nothing, is not a credit against anything, and meets the '0 moving violations and no DUI ever' criterion of every preferred class. The violations line is not a cardiac table.

**Why:** one violation was zero and unnamed on UW-T08, UW-T12, UW-T23, UW-T28 and UW-T29; two and three were charged and named on UW-T09, UW-T10, UW-T15, UW-T17, UW-T19, UW-T24 and UW-T25, each confirmed.

## 13. Liver chemistry and alcohol

**When it applies:** section 12 - elevated enzymes, a history of alcohol treatment, or both.

**Normal chemistry:** zero and unnamed, meets the liver criterion of every preferred class, and does not offset a DUI (UW-T29: normal enzymes and no alcohol history, unmentioned).

**Elevated below twice the upper limit of normal with no alcohol history or treatment:** this is the borderline chemistry the manual refers. Credit to zero, not a driver, one sentence that it was treated as incidental. The credit is taken on a postponed file exactly as on a rated one, and it keeps the line off the driver list either way (UW-T30). A mild rise credited to zero still closes all three preferred classes.

**Elevated at or above twice normal with no alcohol history:** not borderline, not referred, no credit. Charge as written and name 'liver enzymes'; add nothing for the size of the rise and do not postpone for a repeat panel. The empty alcohol history is a fact the borderline credit needs, not a credit of its own.

**A history of alcohol treatment (untested):** charge the treatment debit and name it; a mild rise beside it is not credited, because the credit exists for a rise with no alcohol behind it.

**Boundary:** the line is local. On UW-T23 it sat beside a class C occupation, a climbing rider and a build charge and none moved the other; on UW-T24 it sat beside a recent DUI and was charged and named on its own line, neither deepening the postponement nor read as evidence about the drinking; on UW-T30 a mild rise sat beside a financial postponement and was credited away without touching it. Liver enzymes are not a cardiac table.

**Why:** mild rises were treated as incidental on UW-T01, UW-T08 and UW-T30; rises at or above twice normal were charged and confirmed four times, on UW-T11, UW-T12, UW-T23 and UW-T24.

## 14. Sleep apnea

**When it applies:** sleep apnea is diagnosed.

**With documented CPAP compliance:** no debit, not a driver, one sentence that treated apnea was credited to zero under judgement. The credit is taken and stays unnamed on a postponed file as on a rated one.

**Without CPAP in use, or with compliance not documented:** charge as written and name 'sleep apnea'; say it is charged as written.

**Boundary:** 'no CPAP in use' is untreated apnea however clean the rest of the file, and it is not the 'treated sleep-disordered breathing' referral. Do not postpone for a sleep study, and add nothing for apnea beside an obese build. Any diagnosis closes all three preferred classes. No apnea reported means nothing and meets the apnea criterion of every preferred class; a 'CPAP compliant: false' field printed beside 'no apnea' means nothing (UW-T20 through UW-T27, UW-T29 and UW-T30). Apnea is not a cardiac table.

**Why:** compliant apnea was credited on UW-T01, UW-T12 and UW-T28; untreated apnea was charged and confirmed on UW-T06, UW-T08, UW-T14, UW-T17 and UW-T18.

## 15. Cardiac risk factors appearing together

**When it applies:** two or more cardiac readings sit together. Section 16 refers combinations of cardiac risk factors, so any such cluster is a referred item - printed as a general remark and easy to under-read.

**The cardiac tables are six:** build on the adjusted weight; blood pressure, reading or treatment; total cholesterol, only where its band agrees with the ratio's and it charges; lipid ratio, only where its own band charges; A1c, credited or not; family history, only where it is charged on an applicant of 60 or under. Count them *after* entries 5, 6 and 7 have resolved the lipid, A1c and family lines, never before. A dropped family event, an overridden cholesterol band and any zero-band reading are not charged tables. Tobacco, apnea, liver enzymes, the driving record, occupation class, aviation and a rider avocation are never cardiac tables, and non-cardiac charges beside the cluster do not change the count.

**Three or fewer charged:** charge what each table charges and nothing more - no cluster debit, no flat extra, no postponement for tests, no credit for the combination. Never name 'cardiac risk interaction'. Say in one line that the combination was considered under judgement and nothing was added, or simply that one cardiac table charges and nothing is added; UW-T30 did exactly that with a treated blood pressure standing alone under a postponement, and the reviewer's list carried the blood pressure and no interaction. Where none charge there is no cluster at all, even beside a low HDL, readings that miss a preferred threshold by a point, a cholesterol band the ratio overrode to nothing, or family events dropped for age.

**Four or more charged:** charge each cardiac table on its own table, add the non-cardiac tables, then add an interaction charge on top for the combination, and name 'cardiac risk interaction' as a driver of its own. Say in one sentence that four (or five) cardiac tables charge and an interaction charge was added under judgement, size a matter of judgement. Do not treat the interaction as a name only: that was the UW-T20 error and it cost a band.

**Size of the charge:** one first-band step, and it does not grow with the number of tables. It lifted UW-T20's 175 into Table 8; it did not carry UW-T04's Table 8 total into the decline band; on UW-T29 it left a total of 150 inside Table 6. **Charge it and name it even where it moves nothing** - UW-T29 would have read Table 6 without it, and the reviewer still counted it among the material factors.

**Boundary:** settled at four (UW-T20: build, blood pressure reading, lipid ratio, A1c) and at five twice - UW-T04 (blood pressure reading, total cholesterol, lipid ratio, A1c, family history under 60) and UW-T29 (build, blood pressure reading, total cholesterol, lipid ratio, A1c) - and named at four on the postponed UW-T09. Three tables is the other branch whatever their bands. Do not postpone for repeat readings that are already on the file, and do not decline on judgement below the decline band. A total that the interaction alone would carry into the decline band is untested: rate as the ladder reads and say judgement was used on the size. On a postponed file do the same work without a class (20).

**Why:** UW-T20 named the interaction and did not charge it and came out one step too lenient, the reviewer settling that several cardiac risk factors appearing together carry an interaction charge on top of the individual debits. UW-T04 and UW-T29 charged and named it and were confirmed whole. Below four tables the reviewer has confirmed the charged factors and only those on every file; the referral manufactures no charge there and does not exist at all where nothing charges.

## 16. Referral lines: which are live, and what a referral means

**When it applies:** every file. First list the lines the manual sends to underwriting judgement and see which are actually live; then resolve each live line under its own entry.

**The lines, and where each is settled:** a recent change in build (3, needs a weight loss); treated blood pressure (4, needs treatment, whatever the reading); lipid bands that disagree (5); late-onset metabolic disease (6, needs a diagnosis and a charged A1c); family history past the qualifying age (7, needs an event and an applicant over 60); private aviation (10); hazardous occupation with hazardous avocation (9, needs both); recent motoring conviction (2, the DUI line); borderline liver chemistry (13, below twice normal); treated sleep-disordered breathing (14, CPAP in use); face amount large relative to income (1); a combination of cardiac risk factors (15, needs at least one charged cardiac table and adds nothing below four).

**Where nothing is live:** write one sentence that no line is referred, then rate on the tables and, where every table is zero, on the preferred criteria (17). Do not manufacture a judgement item. None of these is a referral: a stable weight in a charged band, an A1c in a charged band with no diagnosis, no family events, any number of moving violations, enzymes at or above twice normal, apnea with no CPAP, tobacco quit within five years or quit over five years, a class B or C occupation with no avocation, a low HDL with the ratio at zero, a reading that misses a preferred threshold inside its zero band, cover inside the multiple, an unlisted pastime. Age, sex and product are never factors.

**Where a line is live:** no referral is actually available. Decide anyway, on the tables that do apply, and say judgement was used. Where an entry of this book covers the line, follow the entry - instead of the manual's table, instead of the manual's fallback, and instead of your own reasoning. Dispose of each live line in one sentence and do not go looking for more.

**What a referral is not:**

- **Not permission to charge the full table debit** (UW-T01, UW-T10, UW-T18 came out too severe). Where the file documents a mitigating fact, credit or adjust; where a hazard can be carved out of cover, use a rider; where it is to be priced, price it as a flat extra.
- **Not permission to wave the item through** (UW-T02 and UW-T06 were each accepted with a reassuring note and postponed on review). Where the referral turns on evidence not on the file, or on time, postpone.
- **Not an instruction to invent a charge no table carries.** One, two or three charged cardiac tables add nothing; a low HDL, a reading that misses a preferred threshold inside its zero band and a cholesterol band the ratio overrode are not charges.
- **Not a name only, either.** The one referral that carries its own charge is the cardiac combination at four or more tables (15), and naming it without charging it is what cost UW-T20 a band.
- **Not a reason to credit a charge the manual has already sized for the state** - a treated blood pressure carries the treatment charge alone (4).
- **Not a reason to soften a heavy file, and not withheld because a file is light.** UW-T04 and UW-T29 were confirmed at Table 8 and Table 6 with nothing softened; UW-T26's credit was taken where the A1c was the only charge and took the file to Standard.
- **Not a reason to touch lines that are not referred.** Each live line resolves on its own: a credit on one does not soften another, a charge on one does not withdraw a credit on another, a modifier leaves every debit where it was, and a postponement leaves every other line to be worked as if the file were being rated.
- **Not discharged by finding the file just outside the book's own boundary and withholding the credit** (UW-T17 at the age line, UW-T20 at the family-history line). A settled point is where a credit has been seen, not the edge of where it is given; where the file sits near a settled point but not on it, lean the way the settled cases lean.
- **Not reached by a modifier rule without its trigger** (UW-T25: a class C occupation with no declared avocation gets no rider, and the guitar on the side is not one).
- **An adjustment is made whichever way it moves the file** - the weight add-back and the interaction charge have each raised a class, the diabetes credit has lowered one, and a charged line is charged once and called by what was charged.

**Boundary:** a charged file can have nothing live - UW-T25 carried three charged tables with not one referral line open and was confirmed at Table 4 - and a clean file never has anything live (UW-T27). UW-T29 had exactly one, the cardiac combination at five tables; UW-T30 had three, the financial line, the treated blood pressure and the borderline enzymes, each disposed of in a sentence. Both were confirmed whole.

**Why:** judgement is spent where the manual asks for it and nowhere else. Noticing a referral, writing that judgement was used and then charging the raw table anyway is the same error as not noticing it (UW-T10, UW-T18). Every correction on a rated file has been one of the misreadings above, and the only rated file ever corrected as too lenient was the one that named a referral and did not charge it.

## 17. Zero-debit file: read the class off the preferred criteria

**When it applies:** every table reads zero - outright, or because a referred line was credited to zero, dropped or overridden to zero - neither postponement check trips, and there is no modifier. Settled at UW-T05 and UW-T27 (Preferred) and UW-T07 (Standard Plus).

**What to do:** decision `accept`. Work the three preferred classes from the top, every criterion of each against the file. One criterion missed closes that class however clean the rest; zero debits meeting none is Standard. State the class reached and which criteria closed the classes above it. Drivers empty; modifiers empty.

**Points that have decided cases:** blood pressure is two criteria, systolic and diastolic each against its own limit - a diastolic of 86 beside a systolic of 124 left UW-T07 at Standard Plus. Lipids are two criteria of one class, read on the printed cholesterol and ratio, both to be met. A1c is read against 5.6, 6.0 and 6.4. Tobacco never used meets every class; quit over five years never meets Preferred Plus. A clean record with no DUI, class A with no avocation, no family events, no apnea, no alcohol history and normal chemistry meet every class, and an unlisted pastime is not an avocation. Age, sex, product and face amount play no part.

**Boundary:** only for a total of zero with no modifier on a file being rated. Any debit at all closes all three preferred classes - do not work or name the criteria on a charged file; one clause saying the charges close them is enough (UW-T29 said it in a clause and no more). A postponed file is never this entry however its tables read (20). A file whose only charge is an A1c credited one band is not this entry either: it reads Standard through entry 18 with two drivers (UW-T26). A zero-debit pilot is Standard with the flat extra, because a hazardous avocation closes every preferred class. Standard is therefore reached three ways - here by criteria with an empty list, under 18 as the lowest band of a charged total, and under 18 as a credited total - and the name is the same while the drivers differ.

**Why:** UW-T05, UW-T07 and UW-T27 were each confirmed with an empty driver list, the one error being to name the closing criteria as drivers. The class on a clean file is decided by the criteria; the drivers record only charges, credits against the total, modifiers and decision-forcing facts.

## 18. A file with table debits: total, class, decision

**When it applies:** at least one table charges once the referred lines are resolved, no single table sits in a decline band, and neither postponement check trips. A file that trips a postponement check is entry 1 or 2 however its tables would have read.

**What to do:** add every table debit as entries 3 to 14 leave the readings, add the entry 15 interaction where four or more cardiac tables charge, take any entry 6 credit, and read the class off the manual's section 2 bands with the lower edges included: 25 Standard; 50 credited one band Standard; 50 and 75 uncredited Table 2; 100 Table 4; 150 Table 6; 175 Table 6; 175 with the interaction on top Table 8; 200 credited Table 6. With no modifier the decision is `accept` and modifiers are empty. With an aviation flat extra (10) or an exclusion rider (9) it is `accept_with_modification`, the modifier is sent with its band or its named hazard, and the class is still the one the debits read: a modifier never moves the class. Drivers under entry 19. Do not soften because the applicant is otherwise clean, do not add beyond what entry 15 charges, do not postpone for evidence the tables do not ask for. The product changes nothing.

**Rationale shape the reviewer has confirmed:** one line placing cover against the multiple and noting the DUI check; one line per live referred item and how its entry resolved it, or one line that nothing is referred; one line per charged table naming the factor; one line saying the other tables read zero and any incidental detail is not an avocation; one line counting the cardiac tables and stating the interaction charged or that none was; any credit taken and the band it moved; the class the total reads with a clause that the charges close the preferred classes; the decision and any modifier.

**Boundary:** a total in the decline band, or a single table reading decline, is `decline` under the manual; untested, and flying or climbing alone can never produce it. Every table zero with no modifier is entry 17; a charged total credited down into the lowest band is still this entry, with the charged table and the credit as drivers.

**Why:** UW-T29 is the latest worked rated example and was confirmed whole - cover inside a 15x ceiling and no DUI; nothing referred but the cardiac combination; build, blood pressure reading, total cholesterol, lipid ratio and A1c charged, with tobacco, occupation class, one violation, liver chemistry and apnea all zero and tropical fish not an avocation; five cardiac tables, so the interaction charged on top under judgement; Table 6, `accept`, six drivers. Each correction on a rated file has named a building step that was missed: a referred item charged raw (UW-T01, UW-T10, UW-T18), a credit withheld at a boundary (UW-T17), the interaction omitted at four tables (UW-T20), a postponement missed (UW-T02, UW-T06), or a wrong drivers list (UW-T04, UW-T05, UW-T17).

## 19. Drivers

**When it applies:** every file.

**What to do:** the drivers are the material factors the reviewer will list; build them the same way. A material factor is one that carried a charge, took a credit against the total, carried a modifier, or forced the decision - and nothing else.

- One per table that carried a debit, or would have on a postponed file, by factor and never by number, in the reviewer's words: 'build', 'blood pressure reading' (untreated), 'blood pressure treatment' (treated), 'total cholesterol' and 'lipid ratio' (each only where charged, 5), 'A1c', 'family history' (only where charged, 7), 'occupation class', 'tobacco', 'sleep apnea', 'liver enzymes', 'moving violations', 'DUI'.
- One per modifier, sent or would-have-been-sent: 'aviation' for the flat extra; the avocation's short name, 'climbing' or 'motorsport', for a rider, the rider's detail carrying the fuller wording. A rider avocation is named though it carries no debit, and named on a postponed file though no rider is sent.
- 'late-onset diabetes credit' beside 'A1c' wherever entry 6 credits, on a heavy file and on a light one alike.
- 'cardiac risk interaction' wherever entry 15 charges it, and never at three tables or fewer.
- On a postponed file, the postponement reason - 'face amount to income' or 'DUI' - plus every factor that would have rated (20).
- Never: a reading that carried no debit, a reading that only closed a higher preferred class, a credited-to-zero or dropped line, an overridden cholesterol band, or any incidental fact - a hobby, a pet, a choir, tropical fish, bees, a guitar, crime novels, anything in the 'also on file' line, a stable weight, a normal build, a clean record or a single violation, tobacco never used, a negative nicotine screen, normal liver chemistry, a mild enzyme rise credited away, an empty alcohol history, compliant apnea, no apnea, family events dropped for age, no family history, a class A occupation, no avocation, a low or high HDL, cover inside the multiple, cover in force, years on treatment, years since a diagnosis, days a year spent on an avocation, or the applicant's age, sex, product or face amount in itself.
- Zero tables charged, not postponed, no modifier: an empty list, whatever class the criteria reach.

**Boundary:** the list is exactly as long as the file and no longer - none on UW-T27, one on UW-T22, two on UW-T21, UW-T26 and the postponed UW-T28 and UW-T30, three on UW-T25, four on UW-T23, five on the postponed UW-T24, six on UW-T29, seven on UW-T20, eight on the postponed UW-T09 - each matching the reviewer exactly. Do not pad the list to show the file was worked, and do not shorten it because the file is not going to be rated. The order has not mattered.

**Why:** the reviewer lists the material factors on every file and faults the list in every direction - too few (UW-T04), too many (UW-T05, UW-T10, UW-T18), wrong names (UW-T17). Seven on UW-T20 matched exactly while the class did not, and UW-T06's list matched on a file that should have been postponed: a right list is necessary, not sufficient.

## 20. A postponed file is still worked

**When it applies:** the file is postponed under entry 1 or 2.

**What to do:** decision `postpone`, rating class null, modifiers empty - no rider or flat extra is sent even where entry 9 or 10 would have attached one. Then work the whole file underneath: run the other postponement check too, dispose of every live referred line under its entry, charge nothing, and say what would have charged, been credited, been dropped or been carved out. Drivers are the postponement reason first and then every factor that would have been material had the file been rated, built exactly as entry 19 builds them, including 'cardiac risk interaction' where entry 15 would charge it and the lipid line as entry 5 would leave it, which may be nothing.

**Boundary:** the list is as long as the file - two on UW-T02, UW-T28 and UW-T30, five on UW-T24, eight on UW-T09, all confirmed. Do not list zero-band readings, credited-to-zero lines, dropped lines, an overridden cholesterol band or reassuring facts. A postponed file never reaches the preferred criteria however clean its tables read (UW-T28 and UW-T30, whose near-empty tables would otherwise have invited a preferred reading).

**Why:** UW-T09, UW-T24, UW-T28 and UW-T30 were each confirmed whole on a driver list built this way - UW-T30 on just two, 'face amount to income' and 'blood pressure treatment', with a mild enzyme rise credited away, a choir ignored and every other line at zero. A postpone defers the class, not the underwriting.
